Subject: Audit chain exportability & tamper-evidence checklist (RFP section 4.2)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick response during the RFP Q&A. Our compliance team needs a concrete checklist that explains how Redwood produces audit bundles we can use for regulatory review. Specifically we need answers for:
- which audit events are captured (admin actions, model prompts/responses, API tokens usage)
- retention windows and per-tenant overrides
- export formats and whether exports include chain-of-custody metadata (signatures, checksums)
- evidence of tamper-evidence (WORM, append-only, signed manifests)
- time-to-deliver for a full export (SLA) and incremental export streaming options (CDC/kafka, S3)

Can you share a checklist + a representative sample bundle schema? Also note any PII redaction/sampling options. Procurement will need this to complete section 4.2 and to evaluate timing.

Appreciate it — Marta

Hi Marta — thanks for the list. I put together an exportability checklist and a small sample bundle for your review (attached). High-level answers below; full checklist attached as XLSX.

Summary (short answers):
- Captured events: admin config changes, role/permission updates, user/API auth events, model inference metadata (timestamps, model id, sequence ids), and request/response metadata. By default we do not persist full prompt text for customer-managed PII-sensitive workloads unless the tenant opts in; we record hashed identifiers and sampling markers.
- Retention: Default retention is 90 days for audit logs in the hosted plan; Dedicated/Private can configure retention up to customer-defined windows (e.g., 1y, 7y) via policy. Legal holds override TTLs.
- Export formats: Full export bundles are JSONL for events + CSV index for quick lookup. We also provide a signed manifest (JSON) with per-file SHA256 checksums and a PKCS#7-signed bundle statement for tamper evidence.
- Tamper evidence: Bundles are stored in an immutable S3 prefix with versioning and object lock (WORM) when requested. We provide an HMAC-SHA256 timeline signature per daily shard and optional third-party timestamping (RFC 3161) for court-admissible evidence.
- Delivery & streaming: Full historical export delivery target is 5 business days for up to 1TB on standard plans (SLA upgrade options available). We support incremental exports via Kafka topics (self-hosted connector), CDC-style change feeds to customer S3, and an authenticated export API for query-based extracts.

I've attached: auditchain-export-checklist.xlsx (detailed mapping), sample-audit-bundle-20250618.jsonl (sanitized), and redwood-export-sop.pdf (docs link summary).

If you want, I can schedule a short call with Neha (security liaison) and Laura (legal/compliance) to confirm wording for the RFP.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Rachel / Neha — draft language below for the RFP response. I kept it short and certifiable. Please review edits inline and let me know if we can sign off.

Proposed RFP paragraph (for section 4.2):
"Redwood Inference supports comprehensive audit exports that include immutable event records, per-file cryptographic checksums, and a signed bundle manifest to support chain-of-custody requirements. Customers can request WORM-protected export storage (S3 Object Lock + versioning) and timestamped manifests (RFC 3161) for regulatory evidence. Our standard hosted SLA for full historical exports is 5 business days for up to 1TB; Dedicated/Private deployments include accelerated export SLAs and direct S3 streaming connectors. All exports include an audit index (CSV) and JSONL event shards; customers requiring PII redaction may opt into field-level redaction or sampled full-text exports under contract. Legal holds suspend normal retention.

We can provide a notarized export manifest or a PKCS#7 signature for high-assurance delivery at procurement's request; any additional third-party notarization fees would be billed separately.

—Laura Bennett, Legal
"

Minor notes: change "notarized" to "timestamped" if they have stricter wording in procurement. Neha — any technical caveats we should add?

Laura

Marta/Tom — thanks for the ask. Attached are the requested artifacts and the checklist. Below are the consolidated answers we will include in the RFP (section 4.2). If that wording works, we'll paste it directly into your template.

Consolidated answers (to paste into RFP):
1) Events captured: admin actions (role/grants/permission changes), auth events (token create/revoke), inference metadata (request id, model id, response id, start/end timestamps), routing decisions (region, dedicated vs fallback), and system events (scaling, maintenance). Full request/response text is retained only when customers enable it; otherwise we store hashed pointers and sampling flags.
2) Retention & legal hold: Default hosted retention = 90 days. Dedicated & Private customers can configure retention policies per-tenant up to 7 years. Legal holds and eDiscovery requests suspend TTL-based deletions.
3) Export formats & schema: Standard bundle = JSONL event shards + CSV index + signed_manifest.json. Each shard includes event metadata, sequence_id, sha256, and operator_id fields. Sample bundle attached: sample-audit-bundle-20250618.jsonl (sanitized).
4) Tamper-evidence: We provide per-file SHA256 checksums, a signed manifest (PKCS#7), optional RFC 3161 timestamping, and S3 Object Lock (WORM) when requested. For Dedicated/Private we can also support HSM-based signatures and customer-managed keys.
5) Delivery & streaming options: Full export SLA = 5 business days (up to 1TB) on standard plans; accelerated timelines available under contract for Dedicated/Private. Incremental streaming available via: Kafka topics (secure TLS + token auth), direct S3 export (per-day shards), and an authenticated query/export API.
6) PII & redaction: Field-level redaction and automatic PII detection hooks available; customers can request sampled verbatim transcripts for a specified date range. Export manifests include redaction metadata so auditors can verify sampling.

Next steps: If you confirm this wording we'll add the checklist into your RFP file and coordinate signature/attestation options with procurement. Happy to do a 30-min technical walk-through next week.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
